description: Grachtengordel-Zuid 17th-18th c. canal houses (Keizersgracht 596-620, Herengracht, Reguliersgracht): 5-8 m fronts of dark brown brick (often painted black), a stone souterrain with barred lights under a bel-etage reached by a stoop, three axes (two up to 5.6 m, four over 7.9 m) of white-framed sash windows diminishing up the front (3.1-4.0 m on the bel-etage to 1.3-1.6 m under the eaves) on white sills; crowned by a sandstone cornice (a tall frieze, sometimes one pediment dormer) or a neck or bell gable with carved wing pieces, a cartouche and one attic light

match.note: Keizersgracht 596-620 (2023-03-27 strip): cornice fronts and neck gables share the storey grid (souterrain 2.7-3.3 m, bel-etage 4.4-4.9 m, then 3.5-3.9, 3.2-3.5, 2.6-2.8 m), so only the skyline tells them apart (crownMatch); BAG dates many of them to 1650-1720 with 18th-19th c. refronting, hence the wide years. The eaves range is set so that its mean over the four counted storeys (4.4 m) is the measured pitch including the souterrain.

cornice.note: Keizersgracht 616 (175655), 610 (167896): a tall sandstone frieze cornice at 17.0-20.2 m, no dormer in view

cornice-dormer.note: Keizersgracht 600 (165043): one white pediment dormer over the middle axis

neck.note: Keizersgracht 606 (176067), 608 (176066): gable foot 17.8 m, neck about 3.0 m wide rising to about 23.5 m, sandstone wing pieces and a cartouche, one attic light at 18.5-19.6 m

bell.note: Amstel 34 (169281): a bell gable with sandstone wing pieces over a painted-black front, one attic light

stoop-door-left.note: a stone souterrain with barred lights; the stoop climbs to the bel-etage door on the left axis (Keizersgracht 606 and 612 doors on the right are mirrored by mirrorForDoor)

rhythm.bays: 3 axes (2 up to 5.6 m, 4 over 7.9 m)
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: souterrain: 2-3 barred lights | bel-etage: door + 2 windows | upper: 3
rhythm.groundFloor: stoop to the bel-etage door over a stone souterrain
rhythm.roofline: sandstone frieze cornice, or a neck or bell gable with wing pieces
schemaLimits: the door surround (white pilasters and a fanlight) is drawn as a plain door
the stoop's iron railing is not drawn

the frieze cornice is drawn as a 2.4 m entablature (kit maximum); on the strips the frieze with its cap reads 3.0-3.8 m, part of it the cap's projection stretched by the rectification; consoles, dentils and lettering are not drawn
one pane layout (two across, two up per sash) for every storey; Keizersgracht 616's bel-etage has three rows in the lower sash

notes: Eaves of the cornice fronts are the TOP of the frieze cornice (the entablature hangs under the eaves); reviewer eaves pins with countStoreys give that line where 3DBAG reads the roof behind lower
The bel-etage weight is 4.2 (measured 4.4-4.9 m on Keizersgracht 606-616): the compile gate holds every storey over the souterrain to 2.3-4.6 m, and at 18-19 m eaves a heavier weight crosses 4.6 m
